editorial.headline: Private Higher Education: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This private higher-education activity spans diploma to doctoral institutions and remains open to PMA nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
Private higher education under this activity is institutional rather than incidental: it covers privately run education at diploma, undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels, alongside comparable academic, professional, and vocational programmes. Its stated educational orientation is expansive—the universal development of science, technology, art, and the humanities. The category is designed for private universities, institutes, and higher schools, placing the emphasis on an organised higher-education institution rather than a single subject, course, or faculty. It embraces the spectrum from formal academic learning through professional and vocational equivalents while retaining that broad, universal intellectual orientation. The scope also expressly includes establishing private academic higher-education institutions both within special economic zones and outside them.

The prospective registrant is therefore the private operator establishing that kind of institution. The permitted business-scale range is equally broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed. This is an unusually useful point of clarity in the record: each named scale is included, while the category continues to be defined by the character and level of the education provided. A diploma-level provider and a doctoral-level institution can each fall within the stated scope, as can the academic, professional, and vocational forms identified there. For a founder, the disciplined reading is to keep the activity anchored to private higher education and to the institution types expressly named—university, institute, or higher school.

Nationally, the PMA position is clear. The activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. In plain terms, the national record sets the ceiling at full foreign ownership rather than a partial foreign-share cap. The wording matters: this is not an inference from the educational subject matter, the institution type, or its scale. The record explicitly marks the activity open to PMA and separately gives its 100% maximum foreign-ownership figure. Those two details establish the national position directly and leave no lesser foreign-ownership limit to infer from the data. For an operator reviewing the activity at national level, that is the complete ownership message supplied by the record.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. The provincial status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and the record says it is not blocked by the moratorium. The island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. Here, the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—medium-high/high—which the record expressly identifies as outside that moratorium block. A foreign-owned operator can therefore register this private higher-education activity in Bali today; the stated national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The honest Bali picture is not a hidden prohibition, but an activity that remains open for PMA registration, with its Bali treatment explained by the stated higher risk classification at the Besar scale.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this private higher-education activity is not caught by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
